bull_case_summary: Sandisk has rapid datacenter growth and new agreements alongside strong realised revenue. Round two explicitly concedes dominant pricing contribution and preserves only a conditional customer-mix thesis whose through-cycle economics remain unknown.
bear_case_summary: The bear accepts that some opportunity may persist but notes the one-third arithmetic remainder is not identified unit growth. Peak GAAP income, taxes, missing FCF and cooling momentum leave pricing-cycle risk unvalued.
key_points_of_agreement: Approximately two-thirds of sequential revenue growth came from pricing.
The remainder cannot be assumed to represent structural unit demand.
Agreements and datacenter growth do not provide immunity to NAND cyclicality.
Peak earnings and extraordinary historical appreciation are unsuitable valuation anchors.
key_points_of_disagreement: Whether customer mix can preserve enough sustainable cash economics through a pricing reversal to support prospective value.
unresolved_uncertainties: Contract economics, NAND pricing and through-cycle cash resilience.
Tax/nonrecurring reconciliation of GAAP earnings, debt and FCF.
Normalised valuation and corporate-action comparability of the 413-bar history.
